dedupe_keys.name: why ixps matter incident review of ixp failures and national internet resilience ripe labs 2025

description: This RIPE Labs article argues that Internet exchange points deserve recognition as critical infrastructure and supports the case with a review of real incidents. It describes a visibility paradox with three systemic risks: economic optimisation concentrating traffic at a few IXPs, dependence of small networks on a single exchange, and topological centralisation. The incident list covers the 2018 power outage at a Frankfurt facility hosting a DE-CIX switch, a 2021 software fault at LINX, two AMS-IX interruptions in November 2023 totalling over five hours in which traffic fell from 10 Tbps to 2 Tbps, a May 2025 fault at the Milan exchange, and country examples in Kenya, Sudan and Brazil, plus how local peering helped keep partial service in Ukraine. Producer: RIPE NCC's RIPE Labs, published 28 July 2025. Coverage: global, with European incidents in focus. Access: free article, read on the RIPE Labs page. Licence and cost: free; licence not stated. Caveats: it is a commentary with figures quoted without their sources, and no dataset is released. Simulation uses: the incidents give scenario definitions and observed impact magnitudes for resilience studies of interconnection facilities. Related records: Euro-IX IXP database (data-euro-ix-ixp-database) and the PCH IXP directory (data-pch-ixp-directory).
